facts.fact: An isolated system exchanges neither matter nor energy with its surroundings.
facts.quote: an isolated system exchanges neither

facts.fact: Heat and work are not state functions; they depend on the path between two states.
facts.quote: Heat and work are not: they describe energy in transit during a process

facts.fact: A quasi-static process passes through a continuous sequence of equilibrium states.
facts.quote: A process that passes through a continuous sequence of equilibrium states is called quasi-static

facts.fact: The zeroth law says two systems each in thermal equilibrium with a third are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
facts.quote: if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other

facts.fact: A temperature in kelvins is the Celsius temperature plus 273.15.
facts.quote: adding 273.15 to the temperature in degrees Celsius

facts.fact: One bar is exactly 100 kilopascals.
facts.quote: one bar is exactly 100 kilopascals

facts.fact: The molar gas constant R is approximately 8.314 J/(mol·K).
facts.quote: approximately 8.314 J/(mol·K)

facts.fact: In the van der Waals equation, constant a accounts for intermolecular attraction and constant b for the finite volume of the molecules.
facts.quote: The constant a accounts for the attraction between molecules

facts.fact: The work done by an ideal gas in an isothermal expansion from V1 to V2 is nRT ln(V2/V1).
facts.quote: the work done by the gas is nRT ln(V2/V1)

facts.fact: Radiation is the only heat-transfer mechanism that works through a vacuum.
facts.quote: Radiation is transfer by electromagnetic waves and is the only mechanism that works through a vacuum

facts.fact: Water has a specific heat capacity of about 4186 J/(kg·K).
facts.quote: about 4186 J/(kg·K)

facts.fact: For an ideal gas, Cp minus Cv equals R.
facts.quote: For an ideal gas the difference Cp minus Cv is exactly equal to R

facts.fact: Gamma is 5/3 for a monatomic ideal gas and about 1.4 for a diatomic gas near room temperature.
facts.quote: For a monatomic ideal gas such as helium or argon, gamma is 5/3

facts.fact: The Stefan-Boltzmann law says black-body emission per unit area is proportional to the fourth power of absolute temperature.
facts.quote: proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature

facts.fact: The first law, in this reader's convention, is delta U = Q minus W.
facts.quote: delta U = Q minus W

facts.fact: Joule measured the mechanical equivalent of heat with falling weights turning a paddle wheel in water.
facts.quote: using falling weights to turn a paddle wheel in an insulated container of water

facts.fact: Enthalpy is defined as U plus pV.
facts.quote: Enthalpy, H, is defined as U plus pV

facts.fact: Hydrogen and helium warm when throttled at room temperature.
facts.quote: Hydrogen and helium warm when throttled at room temperature

facts.fact: The Kelvin-Planck statement forbids a cyclic device that turns heat from a single reservoir entirely into work.
facts.quote: it is impossible for any device operating in a cycle to receive heat from a single reservoir and produce an equal amount of work

facts.fact: Sadi Carnot proposed the Carnot cycle in 1824.
facts.quote: proposed by the French engineer Sadi Carnot in 1824

facts.fact: A Carnot engine between 600 K and 300 K has an efficiency of 50 percent.
facts.quote: For an engine working between 600 K and 300 K, the Carnot efficiency is therefore 50 percent

facts.fact: In a free expansion of an ideal gas no heat flows, yet the entropy increases by nR ln(V2/V1).
facts.quote: the entropy still increases by nR ln(V2/V1)

facts.fact: Boltzmann's entropy formula is S = k ln W.
facts.quote: S equals k ln W

facts.fact: The Gibbs free energy G is H minus TS and is minimised at equilibrium at constant temperature and pressure.
facts.quote: The Gibbs free energy, G, is defined as H minus TS

facts.fact: The triple point of water is 273.16 K at about 611 pascals.
facts.quote: For water the triple point lies at 273.16 K and a pressure of about 611 pascals

facts.fact: The Haber-Bosch process runs at roughly 400 to 450 degrees Celsius and about 200 atmospheres with an iron catalyst.
facts.quote: a pressure of about 200 atmospheres, and with an iron catalyst

facts.fact: Combined-cycle power plants reach thermal efficiencies above 60 percent.
facts.quote: combined-cycle plants reach thermal efficiencies above 60 percent

facts.fact: Chlorofluorocarbons were phased out under the Montreal Protocol of 1987.
facts.quote: phased out under the Montreal Protocol of 1987

facts.fact: The mean free path of air molecules at atmospheric pressure and room temperature is about 70 nanometres.
facts.quote: the mean free path is about 70 nanometres

facts.fact: Platinum resistance thermometers are the laboratory standard against which other sensors are checked.
facts.quote: Platinum resistance thermometers, whose electrical resistance rises nearly linearly with temperature, are the most accurate and stable and serve as the laboratory standard

facts.fact: The measured residual entropy of solid carbon monoxide is about 4.6 J/(mol·K).
facts.quote: The measured residual entropy of solid carbon monoxide is about 4.6 J/(mol·K)

facts.fact: Linus Pauling estimated the residual entropy of ice in 1935.
facts.quote: Linus Pauling estimated this residual entropy in 1935

facts.fact: Helium-4 becomes a superfluid below about 2.17 K.
facts.quote: Helium-4 becomes a superfluid below about 2.17 K

late_fact.note: Stated only in the last chapter (The Third Law and Low Temperatures).
